theme: Internet-famous animals that are domestic felines of the species Felis catus.
decoy: Famous pets and animal stars of internet memes

members.description: Pet whose permanently downturned mouth made her the face of grumpiness.

members.title: Lil Bub
members.description: Tiny pet with extra toes and a tongue that always poked out.

members.title: Maru
members.description: Japanese pet adored for squeezing himself into undersized cardboard boxes.

members.title: Longcat
members.description: White pet held up in a photo that seems to stretch forever.

members.title: Colonel Meow
members.description: Scowling pet with an enormous, flowing mane of fur.

members.title: Henri le Chat Noir
members.description: Tuxedo-coated pet narrating existential despair in subtitled French videos.

members.title: Smudge
members.description: White pet seated behind a salad plate, looking baffled at dinner.

members.title: Shironeko
members.description: Sleepy white pet photographed calmly balancing objects on his head.

members.title: Choupette
members.description: Pampered Birman belonging to a celebrated Chanel fashion designer.

intruders.title: Doge
intruders.description: Shiba Inu glancing sideways, captioned in multicolored Comic Sans fragments.

intruders.title: Big Floppa
intruders.description: Stern-faced pet with tall, black-tufted ears, beloved in Russian photos.

theme: Internet slang terms that are abbreviations formed from the initial letters of a phrase.
decoy: Short slang terms born in chat rooms, forums, and online games

members.title: lol
members.description: Tacked onto a message to show something was funny.

members.title: brb
members.description: Quick notice that you are stepping away for a moment.

members.title: afk
members.description: Status note that a player is temporarily away from the computer.

members.title: imho
members.description: Modest preface to an opinion someone is about to share.

members.title: tl;dr
members.description: Header for a short summary placed above or below a long post.

members.title: smh
members.description: Expression of disappointed disbelief at something someone just said.

members.title: iirc
members.description: Hedge admitting a claim comes from possibly faulty memory.

members.title: rofl
members.description: Step up from a simple laugh, suggesting helpless, uncontrollable laughter.

members.title: ftw
members.description: Tacked after a noun to cheer it as the best choice.

members.title: irl
members.description: Marks something as happening offline, away from screens.

intruders.title: pwn
intruders.description: Gamer boast for crushing an opponent completely and humiliatingly.
intruders.why: An altered spelling of the word 'own'; its letters do not stand for a phrase.

intruders.title: noob
intruders.description: Dismissive label for an inexperienced newcomer to a game or forum.
intruders.why: A clipped respelling of 'newbie', not an abbreviation of a phrase.

members.title: Nyan Cat

members.title: Badger Badger Badger
members.description: Looping chant of bobbing badgers, interrupted by a mushroom and a snake.

members.title: Dancing Baby
members.description: Diapered infant performs a jerky cha-cha in a repeating loop.

members.title: Salad Fingers

members.title: Llamas with Hats
members.description: Hat-wearing llama calmly explains away a string of disasters to his friend.

intruders.title: Keyboard Cat

intruders.title: Dramatic Chipmunk

intruders.why: Physical hand puppets filmed on camera. The characters look cartoonish but it is live action.

theme: Network standards and tools that encrypt their traffic by design.
decoy: Networking protocols and tools for connecting to remote machines and people

members.title: SSH
members.description: Command-line login to a remote server, usually on port 22.

members.title: TLS
members.description: Handshake layer beneath countless web, mail, and messaging connections.

members.title: IPsec
members.description: Suite acting on individual packets, common in corporate VPN links.

members.title: WireGuard
members.description: Lean VPN tunnel merged into the Linux kernel in 2020.

members.title: OpenVPN
members.description: Long-running VPN tunneling software that can use UDP or TCP.

members.title: Signal Protocol
members.description: Messaging scheme from Open Whisper Systems, later adopted by WhatsApp.

members.title: Tor
members.description: Volunteer relay system that bounces connections through three hops.

members.title: HTTPS
members.description: Scheme behind the padlock icon in a browser's address bar.

members.title: Mosh
members.description: Remote terminal that survives roaming between Wi-Fi and cellular links.

intruders.title: Telnet
intruders.description: Command-line login to a remote host, classically on port 23.
intruders.why: Sends everything, passwords included, as plaintext. It looks like SSH's twin, which is why SSH replaced it.

intruders.title: FTP
intruders.description: Classic file transfer using separate control and data connections.
intruders.why: Sends credentials and files unencrypted; encryption needs the separate FTPS or SFTP.

intruders.title: Gopher
intruders.description: Menu-driven document retrieval system that briefly rivaled the early web.
intruders.why: Transfers menus and documents as plaintext with no encryption.

theme: Systems built for live, back-and-forth text chat between people online at the same moment.
decoy: Early online communication systems

members.title: IRC
members.description: Channels prefixed with a hash sign, hosted on networks like EFnet.

members.title: ICQ
members.description: Israeli-made client with a flower logo and numeric user IDs.

members.title: AIM
members.description: AOL's client known for buddy lists and away messages.

members.title: MSN Messenger
members.description: Microsoft's client with nudges, winks, and custom display pictures.

members.title: Yahoo! Messenger
members.description: Web portal's client with 'buzz' alerts, emoticons, and public rooms.

members.title: Talkomatic
members.description: 1970s PLATO program that showed each keystroke to others as it was typed.

members.title: CB Simulator
members.description: CompuServe service from 1980 modeled on citizens band radio channels.

members.title: Jabber
members.description: Open, federated XML-based standard later formalized as XMPP.

members.title: Google Talk
members.description: Search giant's client of 2005, based on an open standard.

intruders.title: Usenet
intruders.description: Worldwide hierarchy of newsgroups such as comp.lang and alt.folklore.
intruders.why: Posts propagate between servers and are read later; it is asynchronous discussion, not live conversation.

intruders.title: LISTSERV
intruders.description: Software that relays each subscriber's email to everyone on a list.
intruders.why: An email mailing-list manager; messages are read whenever recipients check their mail.

intruders.title: phpBB
intruders.description: Open-source software behind countless topic-and-reply web forums.
intruders.why: Forum threads are posted and answered over hours or days; it is asynchronous.

theme: Viral trends in which participants perform a dance.
decoy: Viral video trends and challenges recreated by huge numbers of people

members.title: Harlem Shake
members.description: One masked person moves alone, then the bass drops and everyone erupts.

members.title: Crank That
members.description: Soulja Boy's 2007 hit with a signature 'Superman' routine.

members.title: The Floss
members.description: Swinging both straight arms back and forth around the hips in rhythm.

members.title: Renegade
members.description: Rapid arm-and-hip sequence set to K Camp's 'Lottery' on TikTok.

members.title: Running Man Challenge
members.description: Jogging-in-place footwork set to Ghost Town DJ's 'My Boo'.

members.title: In My Feelings Challenge
members.description: Hopping out of a slowly rolling car to move along with a Drake chorus.

members.title: Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)
members.description: Silento's 2015 hit that called out a string of named moves.

members.title: Teach Me How to Dougie
members.description: Cali Swag District hit teaching a smooth, shoulder-led groove.

members.title: Hit the Quan
members.description: iLoveMemphis's 2015 track whose smooth arm-rolling routine swept social media.

intruders.title: Mannequin Challenge
intruders.description: Groups hold poses perfectly still while one camera weaves among them.
intruders.why: Participants freeze motionless; music usually plays, but nobody moves.

intruders.title: Ice Bucket Challenge
intruders.description: Participants dump icy water over their heads, then nominate friends.
intruders.why: A fundraising dare for ALS awareness; no dancing is involved.

intruders.title: Planking
intruders.description: Lying rigidly face-down on odd surfaces for a photograph.
intruders.why: A motionless pose captured in a still photo, not a dance.

theme: Platforms whose core content is user-posted video.
decoy: Upload and streaming sites for creators and fans

members.title: YouTube
members.description: Its first upload showed a co-founder standing at the San Diego Zoo.

members.title: Vimeo
members.description: Upload site launched in 2004, prized by indie filmmakers for Staff Picks.

members.title: Dailymotion
members.description: Paris-based upload site founded in 2005 as a European rival.

members.title: Vine
members.description: Six-second looping uploads, discontinued by Twitter in early 2017.

members.title: Niconico
members.description: Japanese site where viewer comments scroll across the screen.

members.title: Twitch
members.description: Livestreaming service that grew out of Justin.tv's gaming section.

members.title: Periscope
members.description: Phone broadcasting app that Twitter bought just before its 2015 launch.

members.title: Bilibili
members.description: Shanghai-based site with scrolling comments, popular with anime fans.

members.title: Veoh
members.description: Mid-2000s upload site known for a landmark copyright case with Universal Music.

intruders.title: SoundCloud
intruders.description: Berlin-based upload site where listener comments are pinned along the waveform.
intruders.why: Built around audio tracks, not video, though it shares the upload-and-comment model.

intruders.title: Bandcamp
intruders.description: Upload storefront where independent musicians set their own prices.
intruders.why: Sells and streams music as audio; video is not its core content.

theme: Software whose source code is released under an open-source license.
decoy: Popular free-to-download software

members.title: VLC media player
members.description: Traffic-cone-branded player that plays nearly any audio or video file.

members.title: Thunderbird
members.description: Desktop email client from Mozilla with a bird-and-envelope logo.

members.title: Audacity
members.description: Waveform editor widely used for recording podcasts and cleaning up audio.

members.title: Apache HTTP Server
members.description: Feather-logo web server that powered much of the early web.

members.title: WordPress
members.description: Blogging and site-building system behind a huge share of websites.

members.title: LibreOffice
members.description: Office suite forked from OpenOffice.org in 2010.

members.title: Blender
members.description: 3D modeling and animation suite that produces its own short films.

members.title: 7-Zip
members.description: Archiver that introduced the .7z format with strong compression.

members.title: Pidgin
members.description: Multi-network messaging client, formerly Gaim, with a purple bird icon.

members.title: OBS Studio
members.description: Recording and livestreaming suite favored by game streamers.

intruders.title: Google Chrome
intruders.description: Minimalist browser from 2008 with a four-color circular logo.
intruders.why: Proprietary. Its underlying Chromium project is open source, but Chrome itself ships under Google's own terms with closed components.

intruders.title: WinRAR
intruders.description: Archiver famous for a free trial that never actually expires.
intruders.why: Proprietary shareware; its source code is not released under an open-source license.

intruders.title: Opera
intruders.description: Norwegian browser that introduced the Speed Dial start page.
intruders.why: Free to download but proprietary; it has never been released as open source.

theme: Websites built as wikis, where visitors can directly change the published pages.
decoy: Online reference sites and encyclopedias

members.title: Wikipedia
members.description: Multilingual general encyclopedia launched in January 2001.

members.title: Wiktionary
members.description: Multilingual dictionary giving etymologies, pronunciations, and translations.

members.title: wikiHow
members.description: How-to guides illustrated with distinctive painted step-by-step images.

members.title: TV Tropes
members.description: Catalog of storytelling conventions, notorious for devouring readers' afternoons.

members.title: Uncyclopedia
members.description: Parody encyclopedia of deliberately absurd articles, launched in 2005.

members.title: Bulbapedia
members.description: Fan reference covering every Pokemon species, move, and episode.

members.title: Memory Alpha
members.description: Fan reference cataloging every starship, species, and episode of Star Trek.

members.title: Wookieepedia
members.description: Fan reference to Star Wars characters, planets, and starships.

members.title: Wikitravel
members.description: Travel guide to cities and countries, later forked into Wikivoyage.

intruders.title: Urban Dictionary
intruders.description: Slang reference where the most upvoted definition tops each entry.
intruders.why: Users submit and vote on definitions, but nobody can edit someone else's entry, so it is not a wiki.

intruders.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica Online
intruders.description: Web edition of a centuries-old encyclopedia first printed in Edinburgh.
intruders.why: Written and edited by staff and commissioned experts; readers cannot change articles directly.

intruders.title: Encarta
intruders.description: Microsoft's multimedia encyclopedia of the 1990s, later also offered on the web.
intruders.why: Produced by Microsoft's editorial staff; users could not edit its articles.

theme: Web search engines that built their index with automated crawlers rather than human-curated listings.
decoy: Places people went to find things on the early web

members.title: AltaVista
members.description: Digital Equipment Corporation's 1995 service, home of the Babel Fish translator.

members.title: Lycos
members.description: Carnegie Mellon spin-off whose black Labrador mascot fetched results.

members.title: Excite
members.description: Service from six Stanford graduates that passed on buying Google.

members.title: HotBot
members.description: Wired magazine's service, launched in 1996.

members.title: Infoseek
members.description: Mid-1990s service later folded into Disney's Go.com portal.

members.title: Baidu
members.description: Beijing company founded in 2000 by Robin Li and Eric Xu.

members.title: Yandex
members.description: Russian service launched in 1997, later branching into taxis and maps.

members.title: AllTheWeb
members.description: Norwegian service from the Oslo firm FAST, launched in 1999.

members.title: Teoma
members.description: Rutgers-born service of 2000, later absorbed into Ask Jeeves.

intruders.title: Yahoo!
intruders.description: Portal begun by two Stanford graduate students in 1994, with an exclamation point.
intruders.why: Began as a hand-built directory of sites sorted by people; its keyword results long came from partners' crawlers.

intruders.title: DMOZ
intruders.description: Volunteer-run service launched in 1998 as GnuHoo, soon bought by Netscape.
intruders.why: The Open Directory Project: every listing was placed by volunteer human editors, not a crawler.

intruders.title: LookSmart
intruders.description: Mid-1990s service launched with early funding from Reader's Digest.
intruders.why: Began as a human-edited directory of categorized sites.

theme: Websites that launched before the year 2000.
decoy: Landmark websites of the early consumer web

members.title: GeoCities
members.description: Free home pages organized into themed 'neighborhoods' such as Area51 and Hollywood.

members.title: Hotmail
members.description: Free webmail service whose original name capitalized H, T, M, and L.

members.title: Napster
members.description: Peer-to-peer song-swapping service that drew lawsuits from record labels.

members.title: LiveJournal
members.description: Journaling community with mood icons, friends pages, and locked posts.

members.title: Slashdot
members.description: 'News for nerds' site whose links could crush small servers.

members.title: Neopets
members.description: Virtual pet site with its own currency and a mysterious island.

members.title: Hampster Dance
members.description: Page of rodent animations jigging in rows to a sped-up whistled tune.

members.title: Space Jam website
members.description: Starry promotional page for a Michael Jordan and Looney Tunes film.

members.title: Something Awful
members.description: Comedy site whose paid forums spawned many early memes.

intruders.title: Friendster
intruders.description: Social network of friend circles and testimonials, later huge in Southeast Asia.
intruders.why: Launched in 2002-2003. It feels like a relic of the earliest web but postdates 2000.

intruders.title: Myspace
intruders.description: Social network of customizable profiles, music players, and a Top 8.
intruders.why: Launched in 2003, despite its dated look.

intruders.title: YTMND
intruders.description: Single-page gags pairing a zooming image, looping sound, and huge text.
intruders.why: Its joke page dates from 2001 and the user-made site opened in 2004; its crude aesthetic mimics 1990s home pages.

members.title: Gorilla

theme: Web technologies first introduced by Netscape.
decoy: Foundational browser technologies of the 1990s

members.title: JavaScript
members.description: Scripting language written in ten days in 1995, originally called Mocha.

members.title: SSL
members.description: Encryption layer for connections, publicly released as version 2.0.

members.title: HTTP cookie
members.description: Small token a site stores to remember a visitor between pages.

members.title: <blink> tag
members.description: Markup that made text flash on and off, widely mocked.

members.title: HTML frames
members.description: Markup that split one window into separately scrolling panes.

members.title: RSS
members.description: Syndication feed originally designed for a customizable portal page.

members.title: NPAPI
members.description: Plug-in interface that let browsers run Flash, Java, and QuickTime content.

members.title: Proxy auto-config
members.description: Script file telling a browser which proxy to use for each address.

intruders.title: <marquee> tag
intruders.description: Markup that scrolled text across the page like a news ticker.
intruders.why: Introduced by Microsoft's Internet Explorer; it was IE's answer to Netscape's <blink>.

intruders.title: XMLHttpRequest
intruders.description: Scripting object letting pages fetch data without a full reload.
intruders.why: Created by Microsoft for Outlook Web Access and shipped in Internet Explorer 5.

intruders.title: Favicon
intruders.description: Tiny icon shown beside a site's name in tabs and bookmarks.
intruders.why: Introduced by Microsoft in Internet Explorer 5 as favicon.ico.

theme: Websites and services operated by nonprofit organizations.

members.title: Internet Archive
members.description: San Francisco library behind the Wayback Machine's snapshots of old pages.

members.title: Khan Academy
members.description: Free lessons that began as tutoring videos a hedge-fund analyst made for cousins.

members.title: Project Gutenberg
members.description: Library of public-domain e-books, begun by Michael Hart in 1971.

members.title: OpenStreetMap
members.description: Crowd-drawn world map whose data feeds many other apps.

members.title: Let's Encrypt
members.description: Certificate authority issuing free certificates for HTTPS.

members.title: Archive of Our Own
members.description: Fan-fiction archive with a famously detailed tagging system.

members.title: Signal
members.description: End-to-end encrypted messenger for texts and calls.

members.title: arXiv
members.description: Preprint server where physicists and mathematicians post papers before peer review.

members.title: Wikimedia Commons
members.description: Repository of freely licensed images, sounds, and media files.

intruders.title: Craigslist
intruders.description: Plain-looking classifieds site with purple links and a .org address.

intruders.title: Duolingo

intruders.title: Coursera

theme: Google products that began as startups Google acquired rather than ones built in-house.

members.description: Street maps with draggable tiles and turn-by-turn directions.

members.title: Google Docs
members.description: Browser word processor with live multi-person editing.

members.title: Google Earth

members.title: Android
members.description: Mobile operating system whose mascot is a green robot.

members.title: Blogger
members.description: Free blog publishing tool whose blogs live at blogspot.com addresses.

members.title: Picasa
members.description: Desktop photo organizer with red-eye removal and simple edits.

members.title: Google Analytics
members.description: Dashboard reporting a website's traffic and visitor sources.

members.title: Google Voice
members.description: One phone number that rings several phones and transcribes voicemail.

members.title: Waze

intruders.title: Gmail
intruders.description: Google's webmail, unveiled on April Fools' Day 2004 with a gigabyte of storage.

intruders.title: Google News

theme: Protocols that normally carry their traffic over UDP rather than TCP.
decoy: Core protocols that keep the internet running

members.title: DNS
members.description: Turns human-readable hostnames into numeric addresses.

members.title: DHCP
members.description: Hands a newly connected device its address and gateway automatically.

members.title: NTP
members.description: Keeps computer clocks synchronized to reference servers.

members.title: SNMP
members.description: Lets administrators poll and monitor routers, switches, and printers.

members.title: TFTP
members.description: Stripped-down file transfer often used to network-boot devices.

members.title: RTP
members.description: Delivers live audio and video streams for calls and conferencing.

members.title: HTTP/3
members.description: Web revision standardized in 2022, built on QUIC.

members.title: RADIUS

members.title: mDNS
members.description: Lets devices on a home network find each other's names without a server.

intruders.title: SMTP

intruders.title: BGP

theme: Malware that spread mainly by emailing itself to victims as attachments or links.

members.title: Melissa
members.description: Word macro virus of 1999 that overwhelmed corporate servers.

members.title: Mydoom

members.title: Sobig
members.description: 2003 worm family whose F variant was the fastest-moving yet seen.

members.title: Klez
members.description: 2001 worm that faked its apparent origin and disabled antivirus programs.

members.title: Sircam
members.description: 2001 worm that leaked random documents from infected machines.

members.title: Netsky

members.title: Storm Worm

intruders.title: Code Red
intruders.description: 2001 worm named after the soda its discoverers were drinking.

members.description: Gaming strip whose creators founded the PAX convention.

members.title: Homestuck
members.description: Sprawling interactive saga about four kids playing a world-ending game.

members.title: Questionable Content
members.description: Slice-of-life strip about indie music fans and their robot friends.

members.title: Cyanide & Happiness
members.description: Dark-humored gags starring simple, round-headed stick characters.

members.title: Hark! A Vagrant
members.description: Historical and literary figures mocked in loose, scratchy drawings.

members.title: Achewood
members.description: Stuffed animals and pets trade eccentric dialogue in California.

members.title: The Oatmeal
members.description: Long illustrated rants about grammar, running, and pets.

members.title: The Order of the Stick
members.description: Stick-figure fantasy adventurers who know they live by tabletop rules.

intruders.title: The Far Side
intruders.description: Single-panel absurdities featuring cows, cavemen, and scientists.

intruders.title: Calvin and Hobbes
intruders.description: A boy and his stuffed tiger go on imaginative adventures.
intruders.why: A newspaper strip syndicated from 1985 to 1995, widely shared online since.

intruders.title: Peanuts
intruders.description: Round-headed kid, a beagle on a doghouse roof, and a pulled football.
intruders.why: A newspaper strip that began in 1950, long before the web.

theme: Software whose name is a recursive acronym, meaning the abbreviation's own expansion contains the abbreviation.
decoy: Free and open-source software projects known by short all-letter names

members.title: GNU
members.description: Free operating system project begun by Richard Stallman in 1983.

members.title: PHP
members.description: Server-side web scripting language created by Rasmus Lerdorf.

members.title: Wine
members.description: Compatibility layer that runs Windows programs on Linux and macOS.

members.title: YAML
members.description: Indentation-based serialization notation popular for configuration files.

members.title: LAME
members.description: Widely used encoder that produces MP3 audio.

members.title: Nagios
members.description: Monitoring tool that alerts administrators when servers or services fail.

members.title: XNU
members.description: Hybrid kernel at the heart of macOS and iOS.

members.title: RPM
members.description: Package manager used by Red Hat and Fedora.

intruders.title: GIMP
intruders.description: Free raster image editor, often suggested as a stand-in for Photoshop.
intruders.why: Stands for GNU Image Manipulation Program. It opens with the recursive GNU, but GIMP's own letters never recur.

intruders.title: GCC
intruders.description: Compiler suite that builds the Linux kernel and much free software.
intruders.why: Stands for GNU Compiler Collection; the G is GNU, not GCC itself.

theme: Internet brand names that are an ordinary English word or phrase with deliberately altered spelling.
decoy: Web companies and apps with quirky, made-up-looking names

members.title: Tumblr
members.description: Short-form blogging platform famous for reblogs and fandom GIFs.

members.title: Digg
members.description: Social news site where users voted stories up to the front page.

members.title: Scribd
members.description: Digital library for uploading and reading documents, audiobooks, and e-books.

members.title: Fiverr
members.description: Freelance marketplace where every gig originally cost the same small price.

members.title: Lyft
members.description: Ride-hailing app once known for fuzzy pink mustaches on car grilles.

members.title: Flickr
members.description: Photo-sharing site beloved by photographers for tags and Creative Commons licensing.

members.title: Reddit
members.description: Link aggregator divided into communities and ranked by votes.

members.title: Dribbble
members.description: Showcase site where designers post small previews of their work.

intruders.title: Tinder
intruders.description: Dating app built around swiping right or left on profiles.
intruders.why: Spelled exactly like the dictionary word 'tinder'; nothing is altered.

intruders.title: Hulu
intruders.description: Streaming service built for next-day TV episodes, backed by major networks.
intruders.why: Taken from a Mandarin word (hulu, a gourd), not a respelled English word.

intruders.title: Slack
intruders.description: Workplace messaging with channels, threads, and custom emoji.
intruders.why: The ordinary English word, spelled normally.

theme: File formats stored as plain, human-readable text rather than binary data.
decoy: Standard file formats for documents, data, and configuration

members.title: CSV
members.description: Spreadsheet rows with fields separated by commas.

members.title: Markdown
members.description: Lightweight markup where asterisks mean emphasis and hashes mean headings.

members.title: iCalendar
members.description: Standard for sharing calendar events and invitations between apps.

members.title: SRT
members.description: Subtitles pairing numbered timestamps with lines of dialogue.

members.title: vCard
members.description: Electronic business card for exchanging contact details.

members.title: LaTeX
members.description: Typesetting system favored for mathematics and scientific papers.

members.title: XML
members.description: Tag-based markup with user-defined element names, used for feeds and configs.

members.title: TOML
members.description: Configuration syntax of key-value pairs and bracketed tables.

members.title: JSON
members.description: Interchange notation of braces, brackets, and key-value pairs from JavaScript.

intruders.title: DOCX
intruders.description: Microsoft Word's default document format since Office 2007, built on XML.
intruders.why: The XML parts are packed inside a ZIP archive, so the file itself is binary.

intruders.title: EPUB
intruders.description: Standard e-book format of reflowable chapters written in XHTML markup.
intruders.why: The XHTML chapters are bundled in a ZIP archive, so the file is binary.

intruders.title: XLSX
intruders.description: Excel's default spreadsheet format, built on Office Open XML markup.
intruders.why: Its XML parts are compressed into a ZIP archive, so the file is binary.

theme: Emoji whose characters were already encoded in Unicode before the 2010 emoji expansion (Unicode 6.0), inherited from older symbol sets.
decoy: Common emoji depicting everyday objects, weather, and marks

members.title: ☎ Telephone
members.description: Old desk phone with a handset resting on its cradle.

members.title: ✈ Airplane
members.description: Passenger jet seen from above, pointing toward the corner.

members.title: ✂ Scissors
members.description: Pair of open shears, used for cutting or snipping jokes.

members.title: ☀ Sun
members.description: Radiating disc used to signal clear, bright weather.

members.title: ❄ Snowflake
members.description: Six-armed ice crystal signaling cold weather or winter.

members.title: ✉ Envelope
members.description: Sealed paper letter, often used to mean a message.

members.title: ☕ Hot Beverage
members.description: Steaming cup, usually read as coffee or tea.

members.title: ⚡ High Voltage
members.description: Jagged yellow bolt used for electricity or speed.

members.title: ✔ Check Mark
members.description: Bold tick used to confirm, approve, or mark done.

members.title: ♻ Recycling
members.description: Three chasing arrows forming a loop, signaling reuse.

intruders.title: ✅ Check Mark Button
intruders.description: White tick inside a filled green square, used to mark done.
intruders.why: Added in Unicode 6.0 (2010) with the emoji set, even though it sits in the old Dingbats block beside the older heavy check mark.

intruders.title: 📞 Telephone Receiver
intruders.description: Handset alone, tilted, used to signal a call.
intruders.why: Added in Unicode 6.0 (2010) as part of the emoji set; only the full desk telephone is older.

intruders.title: ✨ Sparkles
intruders.description: Cluster of twinkling stars used for emphasis or magic.
intruders.why: Added in Unicode 6.0 (2010) as part of the emoji set, filling a gap in the old Dingbats block.

members.title: Caramelldansen

members.title: Leekspin

members.title: Bad Apple!!
members.description: Shadow-art animation of silhouetted characters set to a Japanese doujin track.

members.title: Polish Cow
members.description: Spinning cow model grooves to a Polish rapper's track.

members.title: Tunak Tunak Tun
members.description: Indian pop star appears as four colored clones against digital backdrops.

members.title: Dame Tu Cosita
members.description: Green alien grooves in a Panamanian producer's clip.

members.title: Hare Hare Yukai
members.description: Anime closing sequence whose choreography fans recreated in costume.

members.title: PonPonPon
members.description: Japanese singer's candy-colored clip with floating eyeballs and a surreal set.

intruders.title: What Does the Fox Say?
intruders.description: Norwegian comedy duo in animal costumes ponders a fox's call.
intruders.why: Ylvis sing it in English, despite being Norwegian.

intruders.title: PPAP
intruders.description: Japanese comedian in leopard print jams fruit and pens together.

theme: Web services that operated publicly under a different name before adopting their famous one.
decoy: Major internet companies with well-known founding stories

members.title: Facebook
members.description: Harvard dorm-room directory of student profiles that went live in 2004.

members.title: eBay
members.description: Auction marketplace whose first sale was a broken laser pointer.

members.title: Snapchat
members.description: Photo messaging app whose pictures vanish after viewing.

members.title: Netscape Navigator
members.description: 1990s browser whose ship's-wheel logo ruled the early internet.

members.title: Firefox
members.description: Mozilla's open-source browser, with a logo that wraps an animal around a globe.

members.title: Uber
members.description: Ride-hailing app that began with black-car service in San Francisco.

members.title: Bing
members.description: Microsoft's search service, known for a daily photo on its homepage.

members.title: Airbnb
members.description: Home-sharing marketplace born when its founders rented floor space during a design conference.

intruders.title: Amazon
intruders.description: Online retailer that began by selling books from a Washington garage.
intruders.why: Incorporated as Cadabra, but renamed before the site launched in 1995, so it never operated publicly under that name.

intruders.title: Skype

theme: Acronym-named file types whose letters spell out a description of the content, not the name of a standards committee.
decoy: Widely used media and document types known by their extensions

members.title: GIF
members.description: Looping image type behind countless reaction clips, limited to 256 colors.

members.title: TIFF
members.description: Flexible raster image type favored by scanners and print shops.

members.title: PDF
members.description: Fixed-layout document that looks the same on every device.

members.title: AVI
members.description: Microsoft's 1992 container for moving pictures with synchronized sound.

members.title: SVG
members.description: XML-based drawings that stay crisp at any size on the web.

members.title: PNG
members.description: Web image type with lossless compression and alpha transparency.

members.title: FLAC
members.description: Open lossless audio codec popular with music collectors.

members.title: RTF
members.description: Microsoft's cross-platform document type readable by most word processors.

intruders.title: JPEG
intruders.description: Lossy photo image type that can shrink camera pictures dramatically.
intruders.why: Named for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that wrote the standard.

intruders.title: MP3
intruders.description: Compressed audio type that powered Napster-era music swapping.
intruders.why: Short for MPEG-1 Audio Layer III; MPEG is the Moving Picture Experts Group committee.

intruders.title: MP4
intruders.description: Common container for moving pictures with AAC audio, used by most phones.
intruders.why: Short for MPEG-4 Part 14, named for the Moving Picture Experts Group committee.

theme: Domain names where the top-level domain completes the spelling of a word or brand, so the name reads straight across the dot.
decoy: Short web addresses built on country-code endings

members.title: del.icio.us
members.description: Social bookmarking service that popularized tagging saved links.

members.title: youtu.be
members.description: Short-link address for sharing clips from the biggest upload site.

members.title: instagr.am
members.description: Short address a photo-sharing app used for its early links.

members.title: goo.gl
members.description: Search giant's link shortener, launched in 2009.

members.title: bit.ly
members.description: Popular link shortener whose company is called after this address.

members.title: nyti.ms
members.description: Short-link address for a New York newspaper's stories.

members.title: lnkd.in
members.description: Short-link address a professional networking site uses for shared posts.

members.title: musical.ly
members.description: Lip-sync clip app later merged into TikTok.

intruders.title: t.co
intruders.description: Short-link wrapper applied to every link posted on Twitter.
intruders.why: 't' plus 'co' spells nothing; .co is simply Colombia's code, used here as a generic ending.

intruders.title: last.fm
intruders.description: Music site that tracks listening history, or 'scrobbles'.
intruders.why: Read as 'Last F-M': the .fm stands apart as a radio pun rather than finishing a word.

intruders.title: amzn.to
intruders.description: Short-link address for sharing an online retailer's product pages.
intruders.why: 'amznto' is not a word; the .to (Tonga's code) is just a handy 'to' tacked on, not the end of the brand.

theme: Text faces that are mirror-symmetric: flipped left to right, the face looks the same.
decoy: Upright text faces in the Japanese kaomoji style

members.description: Closed, upturned eyes of pure contentment.

members.title: T_T
members.description: Tears streaming straight down both cheeks.
Flat, unimpressed stare of weary annoyance.
Eyes squeezed shut in frustration or pain.

members.title: x_x
members.description: Crossed-out eyes of exhaustion or defeat.

members.title: ^o^
members.description: Beaming expression with an open, delighted mouth.

members.title: ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ
members.description: Round-eared bear with a small snout.
Squeezed eyes and a wide grin of excitement.
Blank, expressionless stare with no hint of feeling.

intruders.description: Sidelong, shifty glance at something suspicious.
intruders.why: Both eyes point the same way, so a mirror image becomes <_<.

intruders.title: o_O
intruders.description: One small and one wide eye in baffled disbelief.
intruders.why: The eyes differ in size, so the mirror image is O_o.

intruders.description: Playful wink with one eye closed.
intruders.why: One eye is open and one winks, so mirroring swaps them to ~_^.
